voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

lines.text: Three pats. Phone, wallet, earbuds. Every door, every day.
lines.say: [close, rhythmic, a little amused, like a habit you'd never notice] Three pats. Phone, wallet, earbuds. Every door, every day.

lines.text: Except today, the third pat is empty.
lines.say: [quieter, the beat drops] Except today, the third pat is empty.

lines.text: You barely whisper it. And the floor answers.
lines.say: [hushed, breath in it, a small wonder] You barely whisper it. And the floor answers.

lines.text: What if you could find anything ever lost?
lines.say: [low, curious, intimate, a slow build] What if you could find anything ever lost?

lines.text: Down there. With a coin. And someone's ring.
lines.say: [close, almost a whisper, delighted] Down there. With a coin. And someone's ring.

lines.text: Everything anyone ever lost. Even the things your family decided to lose.
lines.say: [lower, a shadow crosses it, slow] Everything anyone ever lost. Even the things your family decided to lose.

lines.text: The rule. Whisper the name of something lost.
lines.say: [plain, exact, leaning in] The rule. Whisper the name of something lost.

lines.text: If nobody alive knows where it is, a line draws itself from your shoes to it.
lines.say: [plain, exact, unhurried] If nobody alive knows where it is, a line draws itself from your shoes to it.

lines.text: One line at a time.
lines.say: [firm, a full stop] One line at a time.

lines.text: So. What do you go for first?
lines.say: [light, a grin in the voice, quick] So. What do you go for first?

lines.text: Home. Your grandfather is looking at the empty hook by the door again. Where the orchard keys used to hang.
lines.say: [warm, tired, coming home out of the rain] Home. Your grandfather is looking at the empty hook by the door again. Where the orchard keys used to hang.

lines.text: Grandfather: Some things stay lost. Keeps the peace.
lines.say: [dry, old, gentle, a habit of saying it] Some things stay lost. Keeps the peace.

lines.text: Every Sunday, the same story. You and your cousin know it by heart.
lines.say: [warm, fond, a smile] Every Sunday, the same story. You and your cousin know it by heart.

lines.text: Grandfather: My brother took that deed.
lines.say: [old man, theatrical, the punchline of a story told a hundred times] My brother took that deed.

lines.text: First test: your cousin's stolen bicycle. Nothing.
lines.say: [dry, deadpan] First test: your cousin's stolen bicycle. Nothing.

lines.text: Of course. The thief knows exactly where it is.
lines.say: [amused, a shrug] Of course. The thief knows exactly where it is.

lines.text: So you try something nobody stole. Your mother's earring. Lost eight years ago, down the courtyard drain.
lines.say: [curious, picking up speed] So you try something nobody stole. Your mother's earring. Lost eight years ago, down the courtyard drain.

lines.text: The line goes up. Up the neem tree. Into a crow's nest.
lines.say: [rising, a laugh held back] The line goes up. Up the neem tree. Into a crow's nest.

lines.text: Her earring. And three that belong to strangers.
lines.say: [deadpan, delighted] Her earring. And three that belong to strangers.

lines.text: Therefore, the bazaar. Rain washes gold into these drains.
lines.say: [brisk, eager] Therefore, the bazaar. Rain washes gold into these drains.

lines.text: But you're not the first one here.
lines.say: [a turn, quieter, wry] But you're not the first one here.

lines.text: In the old gold bazaars, men still sift the drains in the early morning. For the dust the workshops wash away.
lines.say: [low, respectful, unhurried, a real place] In the old gold bazaars, men still sift the drains in the early morning. For the dust the workshops wash away.

lines.text: An old man is asking the whole lane for his hearing aid. You find it in a mango crate.
lines.say: [light, storytelling] An old man is asking the whole lane for his hearing aid. You find it in a mango crate.

lines.text: And the man who comes for it has the face from the folded photograph.
lines.say: [slower, the air changes, hushed] And the man who comes for it has the face from the folded photograph.

lines.text: Madhav: Your grandfather's eyes. Take a mango.
lines.say: [old man, warm, a little rough, holding something back] Your grandfather's eyes. Take a mango.

lines.text: Your great-uncle, Madhav. You say nothing at home.
lines.say: [quiet, careful, a secret] Your great-uncle, Maadhav. You say nothing at home.

lines.text: Then your cousin shows you the news. An old bungalow, coming down. The owner buried her coins somewhere in the compound. Her family has dug for a year.
lines.say: [brisk, gossipy, leaning in] Then your cousin shows you the news. An old bungalow, coming down. The owner buried her coins somewhere in the compound. Her family has dug for a year.

lines.text: You find them in ten minutes.
lines.say: [cocky, quick] You find them in ten minutes.

lines.text: Finders keepers. Right?
lines.say: [playful, a challenge] Finders keepers. Right?

lines.text: The jeweller doesn't pay you. He asks for a bill.
lines.say: [flat, the deflation] The jeweller doesn't pay you. He asks for a bill.

lines.text: There's a law from 1878. Treasure found in the soil goes to the Collector.
lines.say: [dry, exact, slower] There's a law from eighteen seventy-eight. Treasure found in the soil goes to the Collector.

lines.text: In writing. Into the government treasury.
lines.say: [dry, exact, clipped] In writing. Into the government treasury.

lines.text: Keep quiet, and it's up to a year in prison.
lines.say: [low, dry, a beat of menace] Keep quiet, and it's up to a year in prison.

lines.text: You expected money. You get a receipt. And a queue.
lines.say: [wry, tired, a small laugh at yourself] You expected money. You get a receipt. And a queue.

lines.text: So you go for fortunes nobody is coming back for.
lines.say: [bigger, hungry, a new idea] So you go for fortunes nobody is coming back for.

lines.text: Cousin: A man threw out a hard drive. Bitcoin on it.
lines.say: [young, excited, reading off a phone] A man threw out a hard drive. Bitcoin on it.

lines.text: Dawn at the city dump. You whisper.
lines.say: [hushed, cold air, early] Dawn at the city dump. You whisper.

lines.text: The line goes two steps forward. Then straight down.
lines.say: [slow, a sinking] The line goes two steps forward. Then straight down.

lines.text: Since 2013, a man in Wales has asked to dig up the council's landfill. For one hard drive.
lines.say: [low, intimate, steady] Since twenty thirteen, a man in Wales has asked to dig up the council's landfill. For one hard drive.

lines.text: On it, the key to 8,000 bitcoin. A judge threw his case out.
lines.say: [quiet, plain] On it, the key to eight thousand bitcoin. A judge threw his case out.

lines.text: In 2025, he gave up.
lines.say: [softer, a door closing] In twenty twenty-five, he gave up.

lines.text: So, the sea. A wreck off the Konkan coast. The line runs straight into the water.
lines.say: [wind in it, wide, a little reckless] So, the sea. A wreck off the Konkan coast. The line runs straight into the water.

lines.text: Forty-one metres. Down.
lines.say: [almost a whisper, heavy] Forty-one metres. Down.

lines.text: An estimated three million shipwrecks lie on the ocean floor. And not one of them is a step closer.
lines.say: [quiet, vast, slow] An estimated three million shipwrecks lie on the ocean floor. And not one of them is a step closer.

lines.text: Knowing where was never the hard part.
lines.say: [very quiet, a truth, complete] Knowing where was never the hard part.

lines.text: But the one fortune still in reach is at home.
lines.say: [warmer, home, a small hope] But the one fortune still in reach is at home.

lines.text: Cousin: Find the deed. We're rich.
lines.say: [young, mouth full, joking] Find the deed. We're rich.

lines.text: Everyone laughs. Except your grandfather.
lines.say: [the laugh stops; quiet] Everyone laughs. Except your grandfather.

lines.text: And you think: it's in Madhav's house. The line will prove the story. You'll fix this family.
lines.say: [earnest, sure of yourself, a little too sure] And you think: it's in Maadhav's house. The line will prove the story. You'll fix this family.

lines.text: But the line doesn't go to the street.
lines.say: [slower, a frown in it] But the line doesn't go to the street.

lines.text: It crosses the living room. Out the back door. Across the courtyard.
lines.say: [tense, step by step, following it] It crosses the living room. Out the back door. Across the courtyard.

lines.text: To the tulsi he waters every morning.
lines.say: [hushed, stopped dead] To the tulsee he waters every morning.

lines.text: He's at the market.
lines.say: [quiet, careful, alone] He's at the market.

lines.text: In your grandmother's handwriting.
lines.say: [hushed, slow] In your grandmother's handwriting.

lines.text: Let it stay lost.
lines.say: [barely there, her voice in yours, tender] Let it stay lost.

lines.text: The rule held. Nobody alive knew.
lines.say: [very quiet, the floor drops away] The rule held. Nobody alive knew.

lines.text: She hid it. Not his brother.
lines.say: [quiet, shaken, plain] She hid it. Not his brother.

lines.text: You can't look at the envelope. So you look at everything else.
lines.say: [low, restless, night] You can't look at the envelope. So you look at everything else.

lines.text: The oldest earring under this city's drains. Not in the bazaar. Out past the old fort.
lines.say: [rising, reaching, a little wild] The oldest earring under this city's drains. Not in the bazaar. Out past the old fort.

lines.text: The first ship this coast ever lost. Not the wreck you found. Further. Out past it, to open sea.
lines.say: [bigger, breathless, far away] The first ship this coast ever lost. Not the wreck you found. Further. Out past it, to open sea.

lines.text: Every lost thing on Earth has a line waiting.
lines.say: [vast, slow, awed] Every lost thing on Earth has a line waiting.

lines.text: You could walk for the rest of your life.
lines.say: [quiet, a weight in it] You could walk for the rest of your life.

lines.text: Next evening, a power cut. And Madhav is at the gate. Your cousin's video found him first.
lines.say: [tense, low, the story speeding up] Next evening, a power cut. And Maadhav is at the gate. Your cousin's video found him first.

lines.text: Your grandfather pats his pocket. One, two, three.
lines.say: [slow, every count lands] Your grandfather pats his pocket. One, two, three.

lines.text: His heart tablet is gone.
lines.say: [almost a whisper, fear held down] His heart tablet is gone.

lines.text: The whole sea is on your line. Drop it, for one pill?
lines.say: [intimate, a real question, both sides weighed] The whole sea is on your line. Drop it, for one pill?

lines.text: Not in the courtyard. In the lining. Under the pocket he patted.
lines.say: [quick relief, breath out, tender] Not in the courtyard. In the lining. Under the pocket he patted.

lines.text: You give him the tablet. Then the envelope.
lines.say: [quiet, simple, letting go] You give him the tablet. Then the envelope.

lines.text: Next morning. The doors open. You don't pat your pockets.
lines.say: [morning, light, easy, changed] Next morning. The doors open. You don't pat your pockets.

lines.text: Some things stay lost. Keeps the peace.
lines.say: [soft, remembered, his words in your mouth] Some things stay lost. Keeps the peace.

lines.text: Somewhere under that grate is something somebody lost.
lines.say: [gentle, curious, close] Somewhere under that grate is something somebody lost.

lines.text: What would you leave lost?
lines.say: [warm, direct, to the viewer, a smile] What would you leave lost?
